notes: missing: a dated source on the founders' prior ventures and their outcomes; dated sources name only Namik Muduroglu as a founding contributor and give a 23-person team

T03.rationale: 23 team members per the white paper; 12 named contributors committed to the public client repos in the 90 days to 30 Apr, so engineering has some redundancy; no disclosed succession or security/ops leadership.

T04.rationale: In-house team built MegaEVM, the SALT state trie and a stateless validator, open-sourced and externally tested by BlockSec; 10ms mini-block design documented. No public consensus/sequencer spec.

T05.rationale: No enforcement action or misconduct allegation found; the one public failure (Nov-2025 pre-deposit multisig error) was operational, admitted as 'sloppy', with a full refund announced. Registries and court records not searched, so not 4.

T07.rationale: Governance is not live; MegaLabs runs the single sequencer and can adjust parameters through multisig; decentralisation is a KPI with no date, and unmet KPI tokens may later go to an undefined vote.

notes: missing: published treasury/foundation addresses and any treasury report; none found in dated sources. Foundation's 7.5% reserve and VC 14.7% custody not disclosed

T09.rationale: Seed led by Dragonfly with Vitalik Buterin and Joseph Lubin; later backers include Anagram, Kraken Ventures, Maven11, Robot Ventures. GSR and Wintermute are both investors and market makers, which the MM-terms review (M05) must check.

notes: Two claims cross-checked. Supply (10B) matches. Sale demand does not: the MiCA white paper says ~$450M of bids (9x), while the project-promoted and widely reported figure was $1.39B of commitments (~28x). Could be a definitional difference; ask the team to reconcile.

P01.rationale: Real-time EVM execution is a real need for trading and gaming apps, but demand at TGE was shaped by the token KPIs: the 10 qualifying apps were self-incubated and USDM jumped from ~$62.9M to >$300M in the countdown week.

P02.rationale: Public mainnet since 9 Feb 2026 — under 3 months of production at listing; sequencer decentralisation, staking and proximity markets are still roadmap.

P03.rationale: Execution layer is original (MegaEVM with a dual gas model, SALT in-memory trie, stateless validation, 10ms mini-blocks); settlement and bridging reuse OP Stack contracts.

P04.rationale: One high-spec sequencer (100+ cores, TB-scale RAM) run by MegaLabs; BlockSec found DoS paths at the 10B gas limit, mitigated by a 200M compute-gas cap rather than fixed. Liveness limits are acknowledged in the white paper.

P05.rationale: Single MegaLabs sequencer with no described failover; the economic model rests on Ethena's USDM (BUIDL-backed) yield; a third-party bridge provider outage disrupted the Nov-2025 pre-deposit.

P08.rationale: Mainnet shipped on the announced 9 Feb date, but the USDm pre-deposit campaign was aborted and refunded, and the white paper gives conflicting dates for testnet and TGE.

P09.rationale: MegaEVM, SALT and the stateless validator are public (Apache/MIT) with 155 commits in the 90 days to 30 Apr; the sequencer node and token/staking contracts were not found as public repos.

P10.rationale: Developer docs list contract addresses and bridge usage; no published threat model, sequencer spec or admin-key documentation.

S02.rationale: BlockSec's 4 High MegaEVM findings: 1 Fixed, 3 Confirmed and mitigated by a compute-gas cap rather than code fixes; SALT Medium fixed. Spearbit/Sherlock remediation is claimed but unpublished.

notes: contracts_verified not established: the MEGA token (MegaETH 0x28B7E77f82B25B95953825F1E3eA0E36c1c29861) and KPI-staking contracts could not be checked on the MegaETH explorer from this review, and no dated source states their verification status. RF03 stays unchecked. Ask: verified source links for MEGA, staking and buyback contracts.

upgrade_timelock_hours not set: the white paper says multisig changes are 'subject to time delays' but gives no figure; no dated third-party source gives the L1 proxy admin or delay. A live L2BEAT page was consulted but excluded because it cannot be pinned to 30 Apr.

S05.rationale: Admin powers sit in MegaLabs multisigs with undisclosed signers and thresholds; the one observed (pre-deposit) was a 4-signer team Safe whose cap-raise was mis-set to 4-of-4 and executed early by an outsider.

S06.rationale: White paper states fixed 10B supply with no minting function and no pause, but also describes emergency multisig admin functions; not verified on-chain.

notes: No bug bounty amount found; mega-evm SECURITY.md gives a private disclosure channel only.

S08.rationale: No exploit found; the Nov-2025 pre-deposit incident (>$400M deposited, no reported loss) was disclosed within two days with a full refund announced, the refund contract going through audit first.

notes: missing: oracle design of the main apps (RedStone Bolt is named in MEGA-16) and USDM/Aave-style collateral parameters; chain itself uses no price oracle

S10.rationale: Assets enter via the canonical OP Stack bridge (proxy contracts) and Ethena-issued USDM; upgrade admin and delay of the bridge were not established from dated sources.

K01.rationale: At listing MEGA's live use is locking for KPI rewards; gas, sequencer staking and proximity markets are planned; the USDM-funded buyback is announced, not shown on-chain, and MEGA confers no revenue rights.

notes: circulating_supply and market_cap_usd not set: no source dated on or before 30 Apr states the TGE circulating amount. Dated sources give only 'under 10%' (MEGA-07); the documented TGE unlocks (Sonar 500M + Echo 20% of 500M + Fluffle 50% of 250M = 725M, 7.25%) are a lower bound that omits any foundation/liquidity release. Ask: exact TGE circulating supply and its breakdown.

unlock_12m / unlock_90d not computable without circulating supply and the VC (14.7%) and foundation (7.5%) schedules, which were not published in dated sources. Known: Fluffle remainder (125M) vests over 6 months; Echo and team have 1-year cliffs; the 53.3% KPI pool releases on discretionary KPI events, one of which (TGE) was already triggered. Ask for the full unlock calendar.

K09.rationale: Only the team schedule is in the white paper; Echo/Fluffle terms come from third parties; VC (14.7%) and foundation schedules and all vesting-contract addresses were unpublished, and 53.3% releases on discretionary KPIs.

notes: missing: post-claim retention of Sonar/Echo/Fluffle recipients and the Terminal campaign design; cannot be observed before listing
Daily active addresses, retention and fee payers: no dated indexer data; live dashboards were not used to avoid post-listing data.

O06.rationale: The TGE KPI (100k tx per app over 30 days) is easy to farm and was met by self-incubated apps; USDM rose ~5x in the countdown week. No address-clustering data to show an organic base.

O09.rationale: Mega Mafia incubated ~30 apps whose first 13 teams raised >$40M, but builders are mostly programme-funded and one incubated app moved to a rival chain.

notes: Depth, spread, 24h volume and venue share at listing were not captured; spot trading began 11:00 UTC on 30 Apr.
missing: listing-day volume, order-book depth and trade-size data across venues

M06.rationale: Lists simultaneously on Binance, Coinbase (deposits opened pre-TGE), KuCoin, Bitget and ~9 others; tier-1 diligence, but no spot trading history before this listing.

notes: missing: pre-market perp OI and funding on Hyperliquid and Binance; Binance converts its pre-market MEGAUSDT to a standard perp with up to 50x leverage at listing (MEGA-10)
missing: on-chain MEGA liquidity pools and LP ownership at TGE

M10.rationale: MegaETH ran the largest community token sale ($1.39B committed vs Monad's $269M), but pre-market valuation fell from >$6B (Oct) to $1.5–2B, and >84% of 2025 launches trade below TGE price.

notes: No protocol fee or revenue figures published before listing; revenue model (USDM reserve yield) is not yet measurable. B04 (FDV/fees) therefore unscored.

B02.rationale: The planned revenue engine is USDM reserve yield from tokenised T-bills via Ethena — one rate-sensitive source; no fee or revenue figures were published before listing.

B03.rationale: Foundation has said USDM revenue will be used to accumulate MEGA; no buyback address or executed purchases were shown before listing.

B10.rationale: Planned economics lean on USDM yield; 53.3% of supply is reserved to reward KPI growth, and TVL was ~$66M in February — the business has not yet run without incentives.

C01.rationale: General-purpose EVM execution is large but ~95% of TVL sits in 5 chains and 15 new L2s launched in 2025; real-time execution is a growing niche.

notes: missing: two quarters of share data; mainnet is under 3 months old

C04.rationale: Moat is early: latency lead plus the Ethena/USDM partnership and an incubated app set; no retention test against a competitor campaign yet.

C05.rationale: Execution client is open source and forkable; sequencer hardware/know-how and USDM liquidity are the sticky parts.

C06.rationale: Versus Arbitrum/Base: 10ms blocks; versus Solana/Hyperliquid: full EVM equivalence on Ethereum. Monad and other fast EVMs compete on the same axis.

notes: missing: dated peer FDV/TVL/fee comparables for Arbitrum, Optimism, Base-adjacent tokens and Monad at 30 Apr 2026
missing: dated evidence on incumbents' latency roadmaps (e.g. Base, Ethereum L1 block-time work)

C09.rationale: Ethena-co-developed USDM is live (> $300M) and 10 apps are live; investor ties (Kraken Ventures, GSR, Wintermute) are investments, not integrations.

C10.rationale: Adds another Ethereum L2 token to a venue that already lists several; the differentiator is the real-time niche and a large KYC'd retail sale base.

notes: missing: social analytics (engagement rate, bot share) for X/Discord
Holder count at TGE not available from a dated source.
missing: geographic split of users and sale participants; white paper names only EEA host states
missing: disclosed KOL/paid campaigns and the Terminal mainnet campaign design

D06.rationale: Mega Mafia accelerator: 28–30 projects in two cohorts, first 13 teams raised >$40M, 10 shipped to mainnet.

notes: No token-holder governance is live (MiCA white paper G.3); participation is not measurable. Scored under T07.

D08.rationale: Pre-deposit failure explained within two days with a full refund announced; but the regulatory white paper has unreconciled dates and a sale-demand figure ($450M bids) far below the $1.39B publicised.

D09.rationale: Strong backing, but informed criticism: KPIs met by self-incubated apps, thin float, and pre-market valuation down from >$6B (Oct) to $1.5–2B.

D10.rationale: Ethena co-developed USDM; Dragonfly-led with Buterin as angel; BlockSec and Zellic engaged. Endorsement is strong, integrations still few.

L01.rationale: Issuer is a BVI subsidiary of a Cayman foundation; MegaLabs (Cayman) develops; BVI law and courts govern. No named natural-person directors.

L02.rationale: No revenue rights and a MiCA white paper are mitigants; foundation buybacks from USDM revenue, KPI staking rewards and team-run sequencer point the other way.

notes: sanctions_exposure needs the venue's own Chainalysis/TRM screening of foundation, MegaLabs, deployer and top-holder addresses; none are published.

L04.rationale: MegaETH does not itself issue the stablecoin (Ethena does) or custody user funds beyond the rollup; the sale ran with KYC and a MiCA-licensed custodian for EU buyers.

L05.rationale: No litigation or regulator action found in dated press or the white paper; court and regulator databases were not searched directly.

L06.rationale: Standard transparent EVM rollup; no privacy or mixing features in the protocol.

notes: missing: restricted-jurisdiction list for the sale and KPI staking (white paper mentions restrictions only generally)

gates.title: Unrestricted mint controlled by a single key
gates.why: Supply can be inflated at will; every other number in the report is conditional on one person's restraint.

gates.title: Sanctions / illicit-finance exposure
gates.why: Listing would create direct regulatory liability for the venue.

gates.title: Core contracts not source-verified
gates.why: Nobody outside the team can see what users are interacting with.

gates.title: Unremediated exploit with user losses
gates.why: Users are owed money; listing would expose new users to the same counterparty.

gates.title: Active enforcement action against the project or founders
gates.why: Outcome could force delisting or freeze assets after listing.

gates.title: Upgradeable contracts with no meaningful timelock
gates.why: Logic can change under users with no time to exit.

gates.title: Extreme holder concentration
gates.why: A handful of wallets can set the price; order books will not absorb their exit.

gates.title: Unlock cliff within 90 days
gates.why: More than a quarter of circulating supply unlocks shortly after a listing window.

gates.title: No independent audit
gates.why: Code holding user funds has never been reviewed by a third party.

gates.title: Material misrepresentation
gates.why: Two or more project claims contradicted by observed data — the reviewer cannot rely on anything self-reported.

gates.title: Security pillar failing
gates.why: Average security score below 1.5/4 — structural rather than one-off weakness.

gates.title: Anonymous team with centralised admin powers
Undisclosed market-maker terms
gates.why: Token loans and call options are where post-listing dumps are engineered.

gates.title: Insider-heavy allocation
gates.why: Team and investors hold more than half of supply.

gates.title: Mercenary TVL
gates.why: Most deposits are paid to be there and will leave when incentives stop.

gates.title: Volume implausible versus depth
gates.why: Daily volume more than 100x the ±2% depth is a common wash-trading signature.

claim.statement: MiCA white paper: Sonar sale received about $450M in bids, roughly 9x oversubscribed

verdict_reasons: evidence coverage 56% below the 70% needed for a verdict
